precepts.text: Cited as the little sanctuaries the Lord provides in the countries where Israel is scattered, the same as the schools today.
precepts.point: Any task set before our forefathers got done: the Maccabees who were not warriors, the slaves who left Egypt. Egypt was America. If the shooting starts, we know scripturally what happens; the Lord takes care of it.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
“So built we the wall”: all through our history, the forefathers were building. What we are doing today is nothing different from what they always did, and Ezekiel shows the kind of building the Lord gives us while we are scattered.

“Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.” Israel was cast far off and scattered, and the Lord still gave them little sanctuaries in the lands where they came.

When Paul went to Galatia, to Colossae, to Corinth and to Thessalonica, those were sanctuaries, just like the ones you see today. The schools are those little sanctuaries in the countries, and each and every one of us put a hand into building each and every one of them.

So the wall of Nehemiah and the little sanctuary of Ezekiel are the same work. The people built because they had a mind to work, and that mind to work is what leadership has to put into the people now.

precepts.text: If thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light. A leader is locked in with laser focus, and everybody under him becomes the same.
precepts.point: Any task set before our forefathers got done: the Maccabees who were not warriors, the slaves who left Egypt. Egypt was America. If the shooting starts, we know scripturally what happens; the Lord takes care of it.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
The people built the wall because they “had a mind to work.” This is how a leader’s mindset must be, and Christ shows it: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”

A single eye is being locked in, what they call laser focus. Whatever you are locked in on, that is what you are going to see. That is all you are going to see, and that is all that matters.

And when the leader is like that, guess who else is going to be like that? Everybody underneath him. The single eye of the one at the head fills the whole body with light, so the whole camp takes on his focus.

That is why the wall got built. The mind to work in the people starts with the mind of the one leading them.

precepts.text: A wise judge will instruct his people; as the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers. Disorganized camps that talk about rape and build nothing reflect their leaders. When we go to Chicago we are on O'Block teaching, not filmed eating chicken and pizza in the hood at midnight.
precepts.point: Any task set before our forefathers got done: the Maccabees who were not warriors, the slaves who left Egypt. Egypt was America. If the shooting starts, we know scripturally what happens; the Lord takes care of it.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
“A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered. As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” However the leader is, that is how the men under him are going to be.

So when you see these other camps that look disorganized, that are talking about rape, that have not built anything in years, find their leaders, and that is what you will see. When you see us traveling all over the world, building institutions, organizations within the organization, look at our leaders. We are the representation of our leadership.

When we go to Chicago we are not on film eating chicken and pizza in the hood at midnight. How is that a leader of a congregation? You will never see a bishop or a deacon put out a video like that. When we went to Chicago, we went to O’Block teaching the word of the Lord.

Everything rises and falls on leadership. There are cities where the leader was changed and the camp took off, and other places where the leader left and everything fell apart. You are who your leader is. That is why everybody wants to ask the Bishop for the secret sauce, but what they do not understand is that Christ is at the head and we are all following Christ. The Most High is building 144,000 leaders, sealed with the law of God, and nothing they try can stop it.

That is why the people of Nehemiah had a mind to work: the wall reflects the ones leading the building.

precepts.text: Nehemiah answers the mockery with prayer, asking the Most High to turn the enemies' reproach upon their own heads.
precepts.point: This is the pattern for Israel United in Christ today, a people with a mind to work who understand the condition of their people and the mission to rebuild their minds.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

precepts.why:
Before the wall was joined together to half its height, the builders were mocked, and Nehemiah answered the mockery with prayer: “Hear, O our God; for we are despised: and turn their reproach upon their own head, and give them for a prey in the land of captivity”.

He did not answer the enemies in their own coin; he asked the Most High to turn their reproach upon their own heads. Then “So built we the wall”, and it went up “for the people had a mind to work.” That is the pattern for Israel United in Christ today: a people who pray against the reproach and keep building, with a mind to work, understanding the condition of their people and the mission to rebuild their minds.

precepts.text: The builders make prayer to the Most High and set a watch against the enemies day and night.
precepts.point: Their whole plan is to cause the work to cease and keep the city from being rebuilt.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

precepts.why:
The enemies “conspired all of them together to come and to fight against Jerusalem, and to hinder it.” Their whole plan was to cause the work to cease and keep the city from being rebuilt. The builders' answer was twofold: “Nevertheless we made our prayer unto our God, and set a watch against them day and night, because of them.”

Prayer to the Most High, and a watch set day and night. They did not stop building and they did not only pray; they prayed and they watched, because of the ones conspiring against them. That is how the conspiracy to hinder the work was met.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

points: When the enemies' counsel was brought to nought, all returned to the wall, everyone unto his work. Half wrought in the work and half held the spears, shields, and bows.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

points: Everyone with one hand wrought in the work and with the other held a weapon. That is us: nine hours at the job, then the camp or the flyer mission, part-time prophets fighting two battles, and some a third at home.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

points: Be not afraid of them: remember the Lord, and fight for your brethren, your sons, your daughters, your wives and your houses.
That is the charge — the man standing for what is right and holding up the laws of God.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

points: When Sanballat hears that the wall is being built he is wroth, takes great indignation, and mocks the Jews.
One of the heathen rulers rises up against the work, treating the rebuilding of Jerusalem as something to be scorned.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: Before his brethren and the army of Samaria, Sanballat mocks the feeble Jews, asking if they will fortify themselves, sacrifice, finish in a day, and revive the burned stones out of the heaps of rubbish.
He makes his mockery in front of his army, calling the people weak, the same way the heathen today mock the men who go out in one mind to do the work of the Most High.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: Tobiah the Ammonite stands by him and says that even what they build, if a fox go up on it, would break down their stone wall.
The enemy despises the work as flimsy, but the builders answer by praying that their reproach be turned upon their own head.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: The wall is joined together to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.
This is the pattern for Israel United in Christ today, a people with a mind to work who understand the condition of their people and the mission to rebuild their minds.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites hear that the walls are going up and the breaches are being stopped, they are very wroth.
The breaches are the weaker places the enemies expected would fail. When they hear those gaps are fortified, their anger rises because their expectation of failure is broken.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: They conspire together to come and fight against Jerusalem and to hinder the work.
Their whole plan is to cause the work to cease and keep the city from being rebuilt.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: Judah says the strength of the bearers of burdens is decayed, there is much rubbish, and they are not able to build the wall.
Even among the workers the burden grows heavy and discouragement sets in as the enemy pressure mounts.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: The adversaries say they will not be known or seen until they come into the midst and slay them and cause the work to cease.
The enemies plot a surprise attack, aiming to kill the builders and stop the work entirely.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: Nehemiah sets the people in the lower and higher places behind the wall after their families with their swords, spears, and bows.
He arms the people by family and posts them at the exposed places, ready to defend the work.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: Nehemiah tells the nobles, rulers, and people not to be afraid but to remember the Lord, who is great and terrible, and to fight for their brethren, sons, daughters, wives, and houses.
The answer to fear is to remember the greatness of the Most High and to fight for the family and the people.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: From that time half of the servants work while the other half hold the spears, shields, and bows, and the rulers stand behind all of Judah.
The people labor and guard at the same time, knowing the enemies are plotting against the rebuilding.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: Those who bear burdens work with one hand and hold a weapon with the other.
Every builder keeps a weapon ready even while laying the wall, watchful against attack.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: Every builder has his sword girded by his side as he builds, and the one who sounds the trumpet stays by Nehemiah.
The trumpet becomes the signal to gather, keeping the scattered workers ready to unite at the point of attack.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: Nehemiah tells the people that the work is great and large and they are separated far from one another along the wall.
Because the builders are spread out, they need a plan to come together quickly if the enemy strikes.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: Wherever they hear the sound of the trumpet, they are to resort there, for the Most High shall fight for them.
The confidence of the builders rests on the truth that their God fights for them.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: They labor in the work, half of them holding the spears from the rising of the morning until the stars appear.
The people work from dawn to nightfall, giving the full day to the task.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: Neither Nehemiah, his brethren, his servants, nor the men of the guard put off their clothes, saving only for washing.

They are so serious about the work and so watchful that they stay dressed and ready at all times, of one mind to finish the wall, the same way the people are to be of one mind and one spirit today in the resurrection of the people.
